charts.title: Customer Deposits vs Gross Loans & Advances

bookValuePerShare.title: Book value per share
bookValuePerShare.content:
Book value per share (BVPS) is ordinary shareholders' equity divided by shares outstanding -- it excludes the preference shares and perpetual bonds a bank counts as capital but which are not ordinary equity.

For Agricultural Bank of China: the DCF is a book-value/ROE-anchored FCFE model, so BVPS growth (and dilution from the ~RMB160bn core-tier-1 private placement, assumed priced near CNY 7.30/share) is the direct driver of the per-share valuation, not just a balance-sheet metric.

What to watch:

  • BVPS growth outpacing or lagging share-count growth from capital raises
  • Whether retained earnings or dilutive issuance is doing the work

netInterestIncome.title: Net interest income
netInterestIncome.content:
Net interest income is interest earned on loans and investments less interest paid on deposits and borrowings -- the core spread income of a deposit-funded bank, and ABC's largest revenue line (~76% of operating income in H1 2026).

For Agricultural Bank of China: net interest margin has compressed to 1.28% in H1 2026 from 1.45% a year earlier, among the lowest of China's Big Four; this chart shows whether balance-sheet volume growth is offsetting that margin compression.

What to watch:

  • NII growth slowing even as loan/deposit balances keep rising (margin squeeze)
  • PBOC rate cuts and LPR moves that compress or widen the spread

depositsLoans.title: Customer deposits and gross loans
depositsLoans.content:
Customer deposits are the funding base; gross loans and advances (before impairment allowance) are the primary asset it is deployed into. The gap funds the bond and policy-bank holdings that make up the rest of the balance sheet.

For Agricultural Bank of China: ABC's unmatched rural/county branch network gives it structurally low-cost deposits; this chart is the franchise-growth story the valuation leans on when net interest margin is under pressure.

What to watch:

  • Loan growth outpacing deposit growth (funding gap, more wholesale funding)
  • Loan-to-deposit ratio drifting versus regulatory and peer norms

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Agricultural Bank of China Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
